messages:
alejandra: heads up — during the new reranker bring-up I noticed a weird pattern when we score multiple queries per document (multi-query anchor setup). NDCG@10 drops ~3.6% vs single-query baseline, but MRR barely moves. anyone seen ordering effects before?

mudit: interesting. do you mean we concatenate queries or send separate queries and aggregate scores?

alejandra: we concat queries with a special separator: `Q1 ||| Q2` and feed as single context. ordering means Q1||Q2 vs Q2||Q1. same candidates, same reranker. scores and final rank change noticeably for some cohorts.

sara: that's an anchoring effect — model seems to prioritize head query in concat. could be positional bias or softmax saturation in the cross-attention. do we have per-query token length stats?

alejandra: yes — Q1 shorter on avg. I tried swapping lengths and still saw ordering flips. here's a quick log snippet from the eval harness: 
```
config: multiquery_concat, sep="|||", score_agg=first_nonnull
NDCG@10: baseline_single=0.812 -> multi_concat=0.783 (-3.6%)
MRR@1: baseline_single=0.491 -> multi_concat=0.487 (-0.8%)
cohort_longtail: NDCG drop ~6%
```

ben: could be candidate sampling bias too — if our sampled negatives came from a distribution tuned for single-query relevance, anchor signals change. did you try shuffling candidate order before scoring?

alejandra: not yet. I ran two quick variants: (A) keep candidate order stable, (B) squash scores via temperature 0.8. B reduced some extreme flips but NDCG still lower.

mudit: two quick experiments to isolate: 1) shuffle tokenized queries inside concat (break sequence) — checks positional cues. 2) run as two separate queries and combine ranks (max, mean, learned combiner) — checks aggregation method.

sara: also test quantized model — sometimes int8 kernels exaggerate softmax peaking and change relative scoring. try ptq INT8 and FP16 side-by-side on the same eval slice.

alejandra: good call — I ran INT8 (our regular PTQ recipe) and FP16. INT8 had a slightly larger NDCG hit (~4.2% vs FP16 ~3.6%). attaching quick summary in thread.

eval-bot: eval run 1729991001 completed — details: dataset=multiquery-anchor-holdout-v2, seed=42, sample=10k, metrics=[NDCG@10,MRR@1], variants=[fp16,ptq-int8], notes="int8 shows amplified ordering sensitivity"

ben: ok let's formalize: produce a small ablation with these axes — query order (original/reversed/shuffled), aggregation (concat/max/mean/learned), model-precision (FP16/INT8), candidate-shuffle (on/off). keep sample fixed. aim for N=5 seeds to estimate variance.

mudit: I'll add a short eval harness job in the gauntlet: `multiquery_order_ablation.{order}.{agg}.{prec}.{shuffle}`. keep runtime small by using 1k samples per job first.

sara: for immediate mitigation in prod, we can: 1) canonicalize multiquery inputs (sort by recency or explicit priority), 2) use ensemble combiner (score both orderings and average), or 3) treat multiquery as separate requests and merge. each has latency/cost tradeoffs.

alejandra: prefer short-term: run ensemble of both orderings and average scores — cheap to implement and doesn't require model changes. long-term, we should add protocol to canonicalize query order in dataset and golden sets so evals are consistent.

ben: also capture per-query click-weighted NDCG in the report — anchoring might hurt tail queries even if aggregate metrics look OK. add per-cohort breakdown.

mudit: creating eval tickets now and will queue the jobs. tagging @sara for prod mitigation decision if hits persist after ensemble test.

alejandra: thanks — I'll push the small FP16 vs INT8 comparison + order ensemble prototype to the eval dashboard and paste links here when ready. :thumbsup:
